html:
Arnhem Land is a large region in the north-east of the Northern Territory of Australia, east of Darwin. It is named after the Dutch ship Arnhem, which sailed its coast in 1623.

It is Aboriginal land. Its peoples include the Yolngu of the north-east, the Nunggubuyu of the south-east coast, the Alawa in the south and stone-country peoples such as the Rembarrnga. Its western escarpment holds some of the world's richest rock art.

From the 1700s fishermen from Makassar came each year for sea cucumbers; see the Makassan trepang trade. Being remote and poor for cattle, the region kept more of its people and languages than most of Australia. It became a reserve in 1931. In 1963 Yolngu elders sent the Yirrkala bark petitions against a bauxite mine, an early step toward the land rights won in the late 1970s.
